messages:
sanjay: Heads up — we just hit a spike of 502s on /internal/model-fetch in us-west-2a, started ~06:23 UTC. App logs show lots of "connect: Cannot assign requested address" and AWS ALB logs showing target reset.
kelly: Oof. Any change in deploys or traffic?
sanjay: No deploys. Traffic normal, but model-puller batch jobs kicked off heavy pulls.
ops-bot: Alert: NATGW_EPH_PORT_EXHAUSTION detected (us-west-2a) — ephemeral ports nearing 64k on nat-01. Metric: active_connections_per_nat=63920.
elaine: Can you paste a quick ss/netstat from a node in that AZ?
sanjay: Pasted below from a model-puller node (truncated):
```
$ ss -s
TCP:   234567 (estab 120) ... timewait 62000
$ netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
62012
```
kelly: That's nearly all ephemeral ports in TIME_WAIT. Likely client-side fanout to S3/model registry without connection reuse.
elaine: Also check the sidecar config — are keepalives enabled? If sidecars create new connections for every request we'll blow ephemeral ports.
sanjay: Sidecar is Envoy with HTTP/1.1 upstreams, default keepalive seems off in our build.
kelly: Immediate mitigations (short list):
- throttle model-puller concurrency (scale down parallel fetches)
- enable HTTP keep-alive / connection pooling in sidecar and downloader
- add an S3 VPC endpoint so pulls avoid NAT
- split nodes across two NAT gateways per AZ by moving some subnets (costly but fast)
elaine: Also as a stopgap we can tune tcp_fin_timeout/tcp_tw_reuse but that's a bandaid and can hide bugs. If we do tweak:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
```
use with care.
sanjay: I'm throttling the puller workers to 4 concurrent downloads now. Patching sidecar config to enable keep-alive pooling next.
elaine: Runbook checks to confirm NAT exhaustion:
- aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name ActiveConnections --namespace AWS/NATGateway --dimensions Name=NatGatewayId,Value=nat-01
- on node: `ss -tn state time-wait | wc -l`
- on LB: check 502 rate and backend resets
kelly: Longer-term fixes we should discuss:
- central shared egress proxy (connection pooling + caching) for model registry
- use S3 / model registry VPC endpoints to bypass NAT entirely
- split node groups into multiple private subnets each routed to its own NATGW (AZ-local NATGW per subnet)
- reduce outbound fanout in the application (prefix caching of model files)
elaine: I'll open a quick RFC for an egress proxy + vpc endpoint plan. sanjay, can you post a follow-up with updated metrics in 15m?
sanjay: Will do. Early numbers: error rate down 60% after throttling + keepalive patch but still some tail 502s.
ops-bot: Incident update recorded: incident/egress-2003456789 - mitigated (partial) — runbook tasks assigned.
kelly: Thanks team. If we still see >90% port utilization after 30m we flip traffic for half the nodes to nat-02 (manual route change). :eyes:
elaine: Noted — I'll draft runbook steps for the manual route-swap and cost estimate for an extra NATGW per AZ.
sanjay: Follow-up in 15m with new ss/netstat and CloudWatch snapshots.
